response.markdown_report:
The best initial experiment remains **learned relative-position attention bias inside corrected BERT4Rec**. Treat it as an established mechanism adapted to this benchmark, with unverified benefits.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Appended-mask inference makes context weighting consequential; training must remain leakage-free. (2) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile margins and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%; these measured positions motivate discrimination experiments, not validation claims. (3) Users report stale interests and broad resemblance displacing specific present choices. Position offers an imperfect relevance signal, without establishing compatibility or purpose.

**Insights from related work.** (1) T5 directly establishes signed, bucketed, head-specific additive attention biases, shared across layers; our per-layer variant is an explicit difference. (2) BERT4Rec supplies absolute positions; TiSASRec and TemProxRec motivate distinguishing positional distance from elapsed time. (3) MARS motivates fine-grained textual representations, but its pretrained setting differs. (4) CATS motivates useful negative hardness while warning against suspected false negatives.

The framework separates **context weighting → representation specificity → ranking discrimination**: relative-position bias, a jointly trained title/description residual encoder, and mixed uniform/same-model hard negatives. Every option retains one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category.

Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. O/P/U/M/D identify each assessment.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Relative-position bias | 2/6/6/6/5 | O: precise adaptation; P: controlled context study; U: targets stale and broad cues; M: tests weak separation; D: few parameters | O: direct T5 precedent; P: incremental upside; U: indirect intent evidence; M: margins may not generalize; D: backend, export and masking integration |
| Text residual encoder | 4/7/7/6/6 | O: constrained adaptation; P: richer evidence; U: finer distinctions; M: confusing-item separation; D: one joint network | O: substantial precedent; P: sparse text learning; U: no ownership labels; M: lexical shortcuts; D: vocabulary/caching complexity |
| Mixed hard negatives | 3/6/5/8/4 | O: controlled mixture; P: reusable objective; U: challenges plausible alternatives; M: targets wrong ranks; D: unchanged serving | O: established mining; P: unstable hardness; U: stale intent indirect; M: false negatives; D: sampling overhead |

At 0% progress, retain relative bias as the smallest identifiable architectural experiment. Zero-initialize signed bucket biases per layer/head, preserving absolute embeddings and bidirectional content attention. It explicitly targets stale-history dominance and broad historical associations outranking specific recent combinations, although neither behavioral improvement is guaranteed.

Prioritize absolute-only versus absolute-plus-relative; relative-only is a secondary ablation if budget permits. Freeze training and checkpoint opportunities. Verify zero-bias parity, bias gradients, reload/export parity, latency and peak memory before training; dense masks may impair optimized attention.

Select using unchanged sampled-candidate macro validation HR@10. Report category changes and, only when existing outputs expose paired user hits, stratified paired-bootstrap uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates/models. Sampled rankings can reverse full-catalog comparisons; intervals do not correct repeated-selection optimism. Record every comparison. Track popularity, history-length and position shortcuts descriptively. Preserve routing, masked targets, appended-mask readout and diagnostic interfaces; never infer ownership, incompatibility or rejection from unidentified items.

idea.description: Add zero-initialized, per-head signed relative-position attention biases to each attention layer of the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Retain its learned absolute position embeddings in the primary experiment. Each category trains and serves exactly one network and one selected checkpoint. This is a controlled adaptation of established T5-style attention bias, not a new positional encoding principle.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two user-facing failures: historical interests overriding recent priorities, and broad historical associations outranking specific present matches. Learned attention offsets let one jointly trained network adjust context contributions without deleting older evidence. At the terminal MASK, offsets distinguish recent from older history; in interior masked examples, signed offsets distinguish both directions. Position does not identify current intent, compatibility, ownership, quantity requirements or duplicate functionality. The model-facing hypothesis concerns weak positive-negative separation in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics: supplied tenth-percentile margins are -0.2872 and -0.1374, and wrong-rank rates are 12.25% and 11.27%. These diagnostics do not identify a positional defect or demonstrate validation improvement. Text residuals remain a promising later direction for specificity, while hard-negative training more directly targets discrimination but introduces false-negative risks. At initial progress, the positional intervention is easier to isolate.

Integrate with the supplied corrected implementation while retaining its existing projections, residual paths, normalization, feed-forward layers, positional convention and masked-target objective.

Prespecify the primary comparison as A: existing absolute positions only, versus B: existing absolute positions plus relative bias. If the shared budget supports a secondary ablation, C uses relative bias with the absolute-position contribution disabled consistently in training and prediction. Do not combine this experiment with text features, temporal features, augmentation, negative-mining changes or loss schedules. All completed arms include all four categories. Run one configured arm per trial, training independently from seed 42 without loading another trial's weights. Never combine their checkpoints or scores. The initial proposal's per-layer bias tables are retained; T5 instead shares its relative-bias parameters across layers. Use 32 signed buckets and max_distance=128 as prespecified component settings, rather than asserting they are supplied baseline defaults. For each direction, distances 0–7 have exact buckets and larger distances use logarithmic buckets capped at the final bucket. The positive-direction zero bucket is unused. Distances beyond the cap share a bucket; record the baseline maxlen and the fraction of pairwise offsets that saturate. Use physical sequence offsets under the baseline's existing positional convention. Position-only bias requires no timestamps; elapsed-time modeling is a separate hypothesis. Preserve unrestricted bidirectional attention over nonpadding keys. Do not accidentally introduce a causal mask.

Install one RelativePositionBias module in each existing attention layer. Its floating additive mask contains learned bias plus negative infinity for PAD keys and is added before softmax without detaching. For nn.MultiheadAttention, shape it as B*H by L by L. The example assumes the existing attention layer uses batch_first=True; adapt only its layout if the baseline differs. With padding already encoded in this mask, do not also supply a redundant key_padding_mask. Boolean True blocks in MHA but allows in direct SDPA; using a floating additive mask avoids that convention mismatch. For direct SDPA, retain B by H by L by L shape and set dropout_p=0.0 explicitly during evaluation. Exclude PAD-query outputs from loss and readout; key masking alone does not zero them. Every row must contain at least MASK or one observed item. idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch
from torch import nn


class RelativePositionBias(nn.Module):
    """Per-layer signed bias; PAD=0, reserved MASK is nonpadding."""
    def __init__(self, num_heads, num_buckets=32, max_distance=128):
        super().__init__()
        if num_heads < 1:
            raise ValueError('num_heads must be positive')
        if num_buckets < 8 or num_buckets % 2:
            raise ValueError('num_buckets must be even and at least 8')
        if max_distance <= num_buckets // 4:
            raise ValueError('max_distance must exceed exact-distance range')
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.num_buckets = num_buckets
        self.max_distance = max_distance
        self.bias = nn.Embedding(num_buckets, num_heads)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.bias.weight)

    def reset_to_zero(self):
        # Call AFTER any baseline-wide parameter initialization.
        nn.init.zeros_(self.bias.weight)

    def bucket_ids(self, length, device):
        positions = torch.arange(length, device=device)
        relative = positions[None, :] - positions[:, None]  # key - query
        per_direction = self.num_buckets // 2
        exact = per_direction // 2
        distance = relative.abs()
        logarithmic = exact + (
            torch.log(distance.float().clamp_min(exact) / exact)
            / math.log(self.max_distance / exact)
            * (per_direction - exact)
        ).long()
        magnitude = torch.where(distance < exact, distance, logarithmic)
        magnitude = magnitude.clamp(max=per_direction - 1)
        return magnitude + relative.gt(0).long() * per_direction

    def forward(self, sequence, dtype):
        # Floating additive mask for nn.MultiheadAttention.
        if sequence.ndim != 2 or sequence.shape[1] == 0:
            raise ValueError('Expected nonempty B x L sequence')
        if not torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).is_floating_point():
            raise ValueError('Attention mask must use floating dtype')
        if not bool(sequence.ne(0).any(dim=1).all()):
            raise ValueError('Each row must contain an observed item or MASK')
        batch, length = sequence.shape
        buckets = self.bucket_ids(length, sequence.device)
        bias = self.bias(buckets).permute(2, 0, 1).to(dtype=dtype)
        additive = bias.unsqueeze(0).expand(batch, -1, -1, -1)
        additive = additive.masked_fill(
            sequence.eq(0)[:, None, None, :], float('-inf')
        )
        # No detach: gradients must reach the embedding table.
        return additive.reshape(batch * self.num_heads, length, length)


def make_bias_preserving_rng(num_heads):
    # Construct on CPU, then let the normal model.to(device) move parameters.
    # Avoid advancing the RNG used for common baseline parameter initialization.
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        return RelativePositionBias(num_heads, 32, 128)


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    # Correct for LEFT padding and internal PAD holes; never count-1.
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions[None, :].expand_as(sequence)
    last = last.masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Empty sequence')
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    return features[rows, last]


def check_bias_gradients(model):
    # Invoke AFTER backward on a representative nonsymmetric supervised batch.
    # A degenerate batch may require a better diagnostic batch.
    checked = 0
    for name, module in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(module, RelativePositionBias):
            gradient = module.bias.weight.grad
            if gradient is None or not bool(torch.isfinite(gradient).all()):
                raise RuntimeError('Missing/nonfinite bias gradient: ' + name)
            if not bool(gradient.ne(0).any()):
                raise RuntimeError('No used bias gradient on probe batch: ' + name)
            checked += 1
    if checked == 0:
        raise RuntimeError('No relative bias modules installed')

#
# PRIMARY ARM: retain absolute positions and add relative bias.
# CONTROL: supplied unchanged absolute-position BERT4Rec.
# OPTIONAL SECONDARY ARM: relative bias with absolute contribution disabled.
# Each independent trial trains one arm, all four categories, seed 42;

originality.positive: The prespecified absolute-only versus absolute-plus-relative comparison isolates a concrete context-weighting intervention within corrected BERT4Rec.
originality.negative: T5 directly establishes signed bucketed head-specific scalar attention biases. Per-layer rather than shared tables do not establish a novel modeling contribution.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could guide later observed-time or content-conditioned context weighting within one jointly trained network.
future_potential.negative: The intervention is incremental, its user-facing mechanism is indirect, and existing absolute embeddings may already capture sufficient positional information.

code_difficulty.positive: The component adds few parameters, needs no new data and retains one model and the existing scoring interface.
code_difficulty.negative: Learnable mask backend support, gradient verification, initialization parity, dense-mask cost, predictor generation and diagnostic consistency make integration moderately demanding.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the retained bidirectional masked-item backbone with learned absolute position embeddings.
Supports masked-target training and appended-mask next-item inference.
limitations: Does not establish that relative-position bias improves the pinned four-category benchmark.
Interior reconstruction and terminal next-item prediction provide different context geometries.

related_work.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
contributions: Direct prior art for learned head-specific scalar biases added to attention logits using signed relative-distance buckets.
Uses exact nearby offsets and logarithmically grouped larger distances, with bias parameters shared across layers.
limitations: Its text-transfer setting does not establish recommendation gains.
The proposed per-layer tables differ from T5's layer-sharing choice; this difference is not demonstrated novelty.

related_work.title: TiSASRec: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides recommendation-specific precedent combining absolute positions with pairwise elapsed-time representations.
Clarifies that temporal distance can distinguish interactions with the same sequence-index distance.
limitations: Elapsed-time representations differ from the proposed scalar position-only bias.
Does not establish effectiveness for this masked-target BERT4Rec benchmark.

related_work.title: TemProxRec
contributions: The supplied summary describes absolute and relative temporal/positional embeddings and temporally informed contrastive learning.
Motivates testing context-distance information inside attention.
limitations: The position-only experiment omits its temporal and contrastive mechanisms.
Its setting does not establish effectiveness under the supplied evaluator.

related_work.title: MARS
contributions: The supplied summary motivates preserving multiple attribute-aware representations for finer candidate matching.
Supports considering a jointly trained text residual as a later representation-specificity experiment.
limitations: Its pretrained-language-model setting differs from the permitted from-scratch experiment.
Textual attributes cannot establish ownership, compatibility or present purpose.

related_work.title: CATS
contributions: The supplied summary describes cluster-aware adaptive negative sampling and BERT4Rec experiments.
Motivates separating useful hardness from suspected false-negative concentration.
limitations: Reported results concern other datasets.
Unobserved items remain uncertain negatives, and harder training margins alone do not demonstrate validation gains.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons, including reversals in expectation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the mandated benchmark as a fixed selection protocol.
Does not supply a full-catalog performance estimate for this experiment.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection optimism from optimizing model choices against finite validation measurements.
Supports recording comparisons and treating adaptively selected small gains cautiously.
limitations: Does not quantify the selection bias of this particular search.
Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not remove adaptive-selection optimism.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents bootstrap confidence intervals and paired resampling.
Supports resampling corresponding user outcomes together within category.
limitations: Requires paired per-user outcomes that may not be exposed by existing host outputs.
User bootstrap uncertainty excludes training and candidate-resampling variability.

related_work.title: PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Documents additive floating attention masks with L by L or B*H by L by L shape.
Documents mask type requirements and need_weights=False for optimized attention paths.
limitations: API support does not establish gradient behavior, latency or memory use for the installed backend and workload.

Describes backend selection and controls for investigating fused implementation eligibility.
